overview: This 52-page file brings together U.S. diplomatic records from 1932–1939 concerning Japanese intelligence gathering, espionage, covert influence, and propaganda in China. Its early documents report suspected military procurement, intelligence organizations linked to the South Manchuria Railway and Japanese Army, approaches to journalists and foreign experts, espionage arrests, and allegations designed to discredit American and other foreign involvement in China. The later and most substantial material documents Japanese-sponsored propaganda in occupied Wuhan and Canton, especially its increasingly anti-British message, its attacks on Chiang Kai-shek, and its promotion of Sino-Japanese cooperation and a Japanese-led “New Order” in East Asia.
interest: Translated occupation propaganda aimed at Chinese, including anti-British appeals, plus American reports on suspected espionage and media manipulation.
